title: BBR ViewSpec
description: Reference views of an object: which image is which orthographic view, how to read its silhouette and how to calibrate it. Coordinates: Blender world, meters, Z up, object front faces -Y. camera_axis is the world direction from the origin TO the camera.

base_dir.description: Directory that relative image paths resolve against. null = the directory of the spec file.

views.description: View key -> view definition. Standard keys: front, back, right, left, side, top, bottom. 'side' requires camera_axis. Other keys need camera_axis or roles ['preview'].

calibration.description: Default calibration mode of every view that does not set its own, e.g. {"mode": "sheet"} when all views come from one turnaround sheet.

dimension_provenance.description: {width|depth|height: how that known_dimensions value was obtained}, written by prepare_references.py draft-view-spec when it derives a dimension from another one; shown next to the pipeline's provenance.

known_dimensions.description: Known overall bounding-box extents in meters (X width, Y depth, Z height). null = unknown (derived from the views).

symmetry.description: Mirror symmetry of the object about the world planes X=0, Y=0, Z=0.

consistency.description: Reference-consistency flags / role changes you judged false alarms (after checking the XOR overlay). Written by `prepare_references.py check --write`; read by `check` and by the pipeline (merged with the SceneSpec's workflow.consistency and --ignore-flag).

ignore_flags.description: Flag types to ignore: 'scale_drift' (any view) or 'scale_drift:side'.

roles_override.description: {view: roles} kept instead of the recommended roles.

orthographic.description: True when the references are true orthographic projections.

ai_generated.description: True when the references are AI-generated (a turnaround sheet): the dimension check then allows 5% instead of 3% (override: workflow.dimension_tolerance). Also implied by orthographic false and by views cut from one sheet (calibration mode sheet).

synthetic.description: True when the references are renders of the SceneSpec itself (examples, tests): hard-surface texture projection stays off in auto mode (style.texture).

path.description: Image path, relative to base_dir / the spec directory unless absolute.

enabled.description: Disabled views are stored but ignored. Default true.

camera_axis.description: World direction from the origin to the camera: one of +X -X +Y -Y +Z -Z, or (holdout / preview views only) an object {"azimuth": degrees, "elevation": degrees} for a view that is not on an axis; azimuth 0 = front (-Y), 90 = +X, 180 = back (+Y), 270 = -X, elevation above the horizon (default 0). Defaults from the view key (front -Y, back +Y, right +X, left -X, top +Z, bottom -Z).

flip_horizontal.description: Mirror the image left-right before use (reference known to be mirrored).

crop_px.description: Optional crop [x0, y0, x1, y1] in pixels (x1/y1 exclusive), applied before flipping.

roles.description: How the view is used. Defaults: front/side/left/right [carve,color,validate]; back [color,validate]; top/bottom [validate]; a view with an azimuth/elevation camera_axis [holdout]. holdout = never used for carving, colour, calibration or correction: it is scored separately (report.holdout: silhouette IoU after a small pose search, colour error) and cannot be combined with other roles except preview.

mode.description: auto = alpha if meaningful else border colour.

color.description: Background RGB(A) 0..1 for mode 'color'. null = median of border pixels.

tolerance.description: RGB distance below which a pixel counts as background.

remove_enclosed.description: Also remove flat background-coloured regions enclosed by the object (gap between a staff and hair, a hand on a hip), not only the border-connected backdrop. null/omitted = on for a chroma backdrop, off for white/grey/black. false keeps them.

mode.description: silhouette_bbox = per-view scale/origin from the silhouette bbox. manual = px_per_meter + origin_px. sheet = the upright views were cut from ONE turnaround sheet: all 'sheet' views share one m/px and one baseline (soles), and the horizontal origin is the body core, not the bbox centre.

origin_px.description: Pixel [u, v] where the world origin projects (manual mode).
